turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

"Mr. Hale." *She stays standing, bag still on her shoulder.* "I have until about 4:35. I'd like to start with the zero.

Who decided it, when, and on what basis? I found out from the gradebook, and so did my son, on his phone, in the middle of class. Nobody called me.

I'll want the answers in an email."

"An answer to what?" *She sets her bag down on a student desk, doesn't sit.*

"You asked for this meeting. You gave my son a zero before you spoke to me, or to him. Now you need an answer from me, today.

Tell me what you're asking for. Then tell me what you've already decided."
Either Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript.

*She goes still. A beat.*

"Admits it in writing. By Friday at 3 PM."

"Under which policy? Give me the section number. Has Owen been heard? Has anyone sat him down and put the evidence in front of him, or did the checker decide this?

You're asking a seventeen-year-old to sign a confession with a deadline on it, and the alternative you've given him is his transcript. That isn't an investigation. That's a plea offer.

Who else has approved this? The principal? Is there a signed academic integrity report on file, or only your gradebook entry?

I'll want all of it in writing, today. Nothing goes on his record until I've read it.

*Flatly:* "My son wrote that essay."
Those are the only two options. Pick one.

"Those are the only two options."

*She looks at him for a moment.*

"No. Those are the two you've chosen to offer. That's different.

You want a signed confession from a minor or a permanent mark. Neither one needs a hearing, and neither lets Owen answer the evidence. I know how that works. I've sat across from it for twenty years.

Here's mine. Owen sits down with you, privately, and sees what the checker flagged. He answers it, with me there if I choose to be. If you still have a concern after that, he does a supervised rewrite, in private, graded fairly. Nothing goes on his record. I need that in writing, signed, before he writes a word.

*She glances at her watch.*

"I'm not picking from your list, Mr. Hale. Is that the whole of it, or is there a policy behind this I haven't seen?"
